explanation.en:
# Āvaraṇa 1 · Bhūpura — Trailokya-mohana

The square rampart is the boundary between ordinary space and sacred space — "earth-city," the manifest world. Its three lines are worshipped as three distinct populations, which is why bhūpura engravings are so text-dense:

Outer line — the ten siddhis (सिद्धि, attainments), engraved near the gates on this plate (you can see अणिमासिद्धिः at the bottom gate):
# Āvaraṇa 2 · 16 petals — Sarvāśā-paripūraka
# Āvaraṇa 3 · 8 petals — Sarva-saṁkṣobhaṇa
# Āvaraṇa 4 · 14 triangles — Sarva-saubhāgya-dāyaka
# Āvaraṇa 5 · outer 10 — Sarvārtha-sādhaka
# Āvaraṇa 6 · inner 10 triangles — Sarva-rakṣā-kara
# Āvaraṇa 7 · 8 triangles — Sarva-roga-hara
# Āvaraṇa 8 · central triangle — Sarva-siddhi-prada
# Āvaraṇa 9 · bindu — Sarvānanda-maya
The engraved title of the plate. "Śrī" is both an honorific and a name of Lakṣmī / Tripurasundarī; "yantram" means instrument or device — a geometric support for meditation and worship.

content.devanagari: ॐ श्रीं ह्रीं श्रीं कमले कमलालये प्रसीद प्रसीद श्रीं ह्रीं श्रीं महालक्ष्म्यै नमः ॥
content.iast: oṁ śrīṁ hrīṁ śrīṁ kamale kamalālaye prasīda prasīda śrīṁ hrīṁ śrīṁ mahālakṣmyai namaḥ

translation.en: Oṁ. Śrīṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ. O Kamalā, dweller in the lotus, be gracious, be gracious. Śrīṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ. Salutations to Mahālakṣmī.

explanation.en: The Mahālakṣmī mantra, engraved as the closing dedication of the plate. It is built around the bīja (seed) syllables śrīṁ (Lakṣmī) and hrīṁ (Bhuvaneśvarī / the creative māyā-śakti), addressed to the goddess as Kamalā, "she of the lotus." Traditionally recited for abundance and grace.

content.iast:
sindūrāruṇa-vigrahāṁ trinayanāṁ māṇikya-mauli-sphurat-
tārā-nāyaka-śekharāṁ smita-mukhīm āpīna-vakṣoruhām ।

translation.en: Her form red as vermilion, three-eyed, her ruby diadem gleaming, crested with the moon — lord of the stars — her face smiling, her bosom full…

explanation.en: The first half of the classic dhyāna-śloka (visualization verse) of Tripurasundarī, the deity of the Śrī Yantra. The verse continues in the bottom-right corner of the plate. Reciting it, the practitioner builds the goddess's image in the mind before worship of the yantra.

content.iast:
pāṇibhyām alipūrṇa-ratna-caṣakaṁ raktotpalaṁ bibhratīṁ
saumyāṁ ratna-ghaṭa-stha-rakta-caraṇāṁ dhyāyet parām ambikām ॥

translation.en: …holding in her two hands a jeweled cup brimming with nectar and a red lotus, gentle, her red feet resting upon a pot of jewels — thus should one meditate on the supreme Mother.

explanation.en: The second half of the Tripurasundarī dhyāna-śloka begun in the bottom-left corner. Together the two halves form one verse: the complete mental image of the goddess to be held while contemplating the yantra.

The ninth and innermost āvaraṇa, the Sarvānanda-maya cakra — "formed of all bliss." The bindu is the seat of Mahātripurasundarī herself, the undivided source from which the nine interlocking triangles and all outer enclosures emanate. In śrī-vidyā practice the eye is led inward through the āvaraṇas to rest here. On this plate the bīja syllables klīṁ and sauḥ are engraved beside the bindu.

One of 16 syllables engraved in the breaks of the bhūpura's middle line. They are not bīja mantras: read clockwise around the square they form a single caption naming this āvaraṇa, the way a book labels a chapter.

**प्रथमावरणम् श्रीत्रैलोक्यमोहनचक्रं**  
*prathamāvaraṇam śrī-trailokya-mohana-cakraṁ*  
"The first āvaraṇa — the Śrī Trailokya-mohana cakra, the wheel that enchants the three worlds."

The sequence starts on the bottom (west) side just past the bottom-right corner and runs clockwise:  
प्र · थ · *west gate* · मा · व · र · ण · म · *north gate* · श्री · त्रै · लो · क्य · *east gate* · मो · ह · न · *south gate* · च · क्रं.  
This syllable is **मो**, the 12th.

Every syllable is engraved with its top pointing outward, so the caption reads upright when you stand at the bindu and turn clockwise. That is why the bottom-side syllables look upside down on the plate (थ resembles the numeral ८, प्र a Latin K) and the left and right sides look sideways.
